title: AI’s impact on jobs market may take 25 years to play out, says Microsoft chief Brad Smith
key_facts: Brad Smith, vice chair and president of Microsoft, spoke at the International AI Summit at the RDS in Dublin and to the Irish Times podcast Inside Business
He said AI's effect on jobs could take up to 25 years to play out
He said "So far we are not seeing AI displace a lot of jobs" but expects new challenges and called for skills training and "creative Government policies"
He said there are "more safety rules for a carton of milk than for the most powerful AI on the planet"
He said he does not want rules that stifle innovation
He expects governments to move first, perhaps starting with incident reporting, and named Australia as a possible early mover
Based on Microsoft research, Ireland ranks third worldwide for share of population using AI, at 49.9 per cent
quote_evidence: So far we are not seeing AI displace a lot of jobs, but I think it would be a mistake to just assume that the future won't create new challenges.
Right now, there are more safety rules for a carton of milk than for the most powerful AI on the planet.
why_it_matters_hint: A senior Microsoft executive says job effects are gradual but need skills and policy planning.
notes: Read in full. Remarks are Smith's opinion and forecast, not research findings.
